cards.text: The LORD is speaking through Hosea the prophet about Ephraim, the northern kingdom of Israel. Ephraim mixes with the nations, and then the LORD reaches right into my kitchen for a picture: "Ephraim is an unturned cake." Friend, I've pulled that one out of the oven, and the only move is a towel over the pan and a straight face.

cards.question: Foreigners are eating away at Ephraim's strength. How does Ephraim react?

cards.text: That's your phone at 2 percent while you keep scrolling like it's fully charged. And it gets worse, because even his hair is streaked with gray.

cards.question: Ephraim's hair is streaked with gray, and Ephraim knows it.

cards.text: Then the LORD says Israel's arrogance testifies against them. Their own pride walks into court and testifies AGAINST them.

cards.question: With their own arrogance testifying against them, Israel finally returns to the LORD their God.

cards.text: So the LORD says Ephraim has become like a silly, senseless dove. My Minty is a dove, baker, so I'm taking this one PERSONALLY.

cards.question: This senseless dove can't settle. Which two nations does Ephraim flutter between?

cards.text: Calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria. That's me at the store hopping between two checkout lines, and somehow I'm STILL the last one out the door.

cards.question: Ephraim is flapping around like a bird. As they go, what does the LORD say He'll spread over them?

cards.text: He'll bring them down like birds of the air and chastise them when He hears them flocking together.

cards.question: The LORD says woe to them for straying from Him, destruction for rebelling against Him, and then this: though He would ___ them, they speak ___ against Him.
When the people wail upon their beds, they are crying out to the LORD from their hearts.
The people slash themselves, and still they turn away from the LORD. What are they slashing themselves for?
The LORD trained and strengthened their arms, and they plot evil against Him.

cards.text: They turn, but not to the Most High. Oh, so NOW the unturned cake wants to turn?

cards.question: They turn, but not to the Most High. What does the LORD say they're like?

cards.text: A bow you can't count on. Baker, that's my oven timer: it says ten minutes and means whatever it feels like.

cards.question: Their leaders will fall by the sword for the cursing of their tongue. For this, they'll be ridiculed in the land of ___.

cards.text: Egypt. The same place that senseless dove kept calling out to, and that's where the LORD leaves it, friend, so let that one sit with you a minute.

findings.problem: The card calls Ephraim 'the northern kingdom of Israel,' but Hosea 7:8 doesn't say this. The card cites only Hosea 7:8 and gives no reference for that outside fact.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card only restates Hosea 7:12 with no Papa Dorin voice at all. It is also the only story card covering 7:12 to 7:15, so this stretch has no personality.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Choosing Egypt over Assyria is a coin flip, since both were set up on card 8 and nothing in the earlier cards points to Egypt. This is the fourth discovery question in the stop, after cards 8, 14 and 17, out of 11 choice cards.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The card tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats card 19's answer (Egypt) and points back to 7:11, so it works as a recap instead of moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card says the dove 'kept calling out to' Egypt. Hosea 7:11 says only 'calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria,' and 'kept' stretches the text into ongoing, repeated action.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
